correctness.rationale: Equal squared moduli put the difference of two coefficient outer products in the real Hermitian sampling kernel, with rank at most two. I independently constructed the measurement matrix directly on a standard Hermitian basis over the rationals and found nullity four. Using that independently computed basis, I formed all sixteen minors of size three and tested each of the four projective charts over Q(i) by normalizing one kernel coordinate to one. The Gröbner basis is [1] in every chart. Thus even the complexified pencil has no nonzero rank-at-most-two point; this independently proves the needed certificate without assuming the frozen pencil coordinates or its four reductions. Equal outer products imply equality up to phase, including the zero case. For the ambiguity at radius two, writing R=|ζ|² and T=ζ², the intensity gap of the displayed pair is 2(R−1)(R−2)(R−4)+4√14(R−2) Im T. It vanishes on the three stated orbits: R=2 on the middle one and T is real on the other two. The distinct odd/even supports exclude phase equivalence. Squared Gaussian norms are integers and the only nonzero orbits below squared radius five have representatives 1, 1+i, 2, so the exhibited design attains the restricted minimum.
residual_risks: The exact chart calculation is for the specified nodes. It does not prove generic stability bounds, minimal cardinality, or any unrestricted radius statement.

value.rationale: Gaussian coordinates and complete rotational orbits give a natural exact, highly symmetric polynomial-sampling constraint. The first three available orbit radii fail, so just counting twelve measurements cannot settle the design question. A universal success at the next radius, paired with an explicit alias at the only smaller candidate, is a meaningful sharp design boundary. Neither a generic frame dimension count nor the prior 12-sample constructions give that information.
residual_risks: No optimal noise constant or practical performance guarantee follows from the radius result.
